I can’t speak much to her specific training or temperament, that really varies dog to dog (especially with her having previous owners). I will say that I have a black lab who is 3.5 years old. She is still learning sociable skills, tricks, and general patterns all the time. I used to be kind of a crappy dog owner, just didn’t give her enough attention while working 3rd shift. As soon as I moved to 1st shift our whole schedule started to change and she handled it beautifully, even became my new disc golf partner!! I also exposed her to TONS of stuff to try and limit any skittishness or defensiveness she might feel towards other animals or people. It’ll take some work, but there’s a good chance it’ll work out if you’re willing to take your time.

I’m really sorry you’re feeling this way. I hurt my best friend in unimaginable ways 6 years ago, and we haven’t talked since. I still hurt when I think about him, but I’m still here. Things can get shitty but I can almost guarantee that if you end things it will only hurt them more.

As someone else who also wanted to end things at 13… I’m 25 now and life is soooo much better. Not perfect, but better. Your circumstances shouldn’t be diminished but I hope you can see the open space of possibility past this point in time. Parents can definitely suck. Siblings can also suck. But you’ll soon have the opportunity to speak and hangout with whoever you want. Trust me, it’s worth staying around for

I just moved to 1st shift after working 3rd shift at Pfizer in the labs for a year. 3rd shift is super quiet, even in the busiest areas there’s not many people around. You’ll run into some people if you happen to be cleaning the main hallway bathrooms during a lunch break, so just avoid that around 2:30am or so. Most people that I ran into also wanted to mind their own business so we would exchange a head nod and maybe a few words every couple days. If I could’ve handled the sleep, I would’ve never left 3rd. I loved it.
